explanations.explanation: Verse 24 says Cornelius, the Roman centurion (Acts 10:1), had called together his relatives and close friends. I think that's a man too excited to keep good news to himself. Friend, if my family lived nearby I'd have called them too, and then I'd have lit the oven.

explanations.answer: The officers of the Italian Regiment
explanations.explanation: That's a fair guess for a centurion, an officer in the Italian Regiment (Acts 10:1). But verse 24 names his relatives and close friends, and it doesn't mention any officers. Sounds more like a family gathering than a staff meeting.
The text never mentions synagogue elders. Verse 24 says Cornelius called together his relatives and close friends. That's a living room crowd, not a committee.
Peter doesn't let him stay down there. Verse 26 says Peter helped him up. Then he said, "Stand up… I am only a man myself." Peter wasn't about to accept a worship he didn't deserve.

Right, Peter helped him up. He told Cornelius, "Stand up… I am only a man myself." (Acts 10:26) If somebody dropped down in front of me, I'd say the same thing, friend. I'm just a stamper with a big mustache.

Peter says the opposite. He tells the crowd, "You know how unlawful it is for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him." (Acts 10:28) He's saying out loud what everybody in the room already knows. Then he explains why he came anyway.

That's it. Peter says it's unlawful for a Jew to associate with a foreigner or visit him. Then he adds, "But God has shown me that I should not call any man impure or unclean." (Acts 10:28) He names the rule, and then he says what God showed him.
Peter says, "So when I was invited, I came without objection." (Acts 10:29) He just says it and shows up. Friend, I've seen grown men argue with a snooze button longer than that.
The text doesn't mention a second invitation. Peter says he came without objection when he was invited (Acts 10:29). One invitation was enough.

explanations.answer: After asking the elders in Joppa
explanations.explanation: Peter never says anything about asking elders in Joppa, a seaside city (Acts 10:5-6). He says God showed him that he should not call any man impure or unclean (Acts 10:28). Then he says, "So when I was invited, I came without objection." (Acts 10:29)

explanations.answer: His prayer was heard and his gifts remembered
explanations.explanation: The man in radiant clothing says, "Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your gifts to the poor have been remembered before God." (Acts 10:31) Both are named in that one sentence, prayer first and gifts second. Both are said to be before God.

explanations.answer: He must pray longer and give even more
explanations.explanation: The man doesn't tell Cornelius to do more of anything. He says Cornelius's prayer has been heard, and his gifts to the poor have been remembered before God (Acts 10:31). That's the message he brought.

explanations.answer: His gifts should be sent to Jerusalem
explanations.explanation: Jerusalem doesn't come up in the man's message. He says Cornelius's gifts to the poor have been remembered before God, then tells him to send to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter (Acts 10:31-32). The only place he sends anyone is Joppa.

He said it plainly. The man tells Cornelius that Peter "…is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea." (Acts 10:32) He gives Cornelius the name and the place. That's about as clear as directions get.

This one's true, and the man gave very clear directions. He says Simon, who is called Peter, "…is a guest in the home of Simon the tanner, by the sea." (Acts 10:32) Name, house and seaside. My own directions are never that good.

explanations.answer: Listen to everything the Lord told Peter to say
explanations.explanation: Cornelius says, "Now then, we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has instructed you to tell us." (Acts 10:33) The whole room is ready to listen. I wish every audience came that ready.

explanations.answer: Hear Peter describe his vision on the roof
explanations.explanation: Cornelius doesn't ask about the roof. He says everyone is there to listen to everything the Lord has instructed Peter to tell them (Acts 10:33). The room was ready to hear whatever the Lord had told Peter.

explanations.answer: Watch Peter heal the sick among them
explanations.explanation: Nobody in the room mentions healing. Cornelius says they're all there to listen to everything the Lord has instructed Peter to tell them (Acts 10:33). They came ready to listen.

Peter says, "I now truly understand that God does not show favoritism…" (Acts 10:34) The word "now" matters there. He's standing in a Gentile's house when he says it. I think that's a man who just learned something big and said it right away.

That's not what Peter says. His opening line is that God does not show favoritism (Acts 10:34). Cornelius says a man in radiant clothing stood before him and told him, "…your prayer has been heard…" (Acts 10:30-31). Favoritism, not prophets, is what Peter names.

explanations.answer: God hears only prayers in the temple
explanations.explanation: Peter doesn't say that. Cornelius was praying in his house when the man in radiant clothing told him, "…your prayer has been heard…" (Acts 10:30-31). Peter's point is that God does not show favoritism (Acts 10:34).
Peter says God "…welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right." (Acts 10:35) Every nation is in that sentence. And Peter says it with a room of Gentiles right in front of him.

That sentence on the card is true, baker. Peter says God "…welcomes those from every nation who fear Him and do what is right." (Acts 10:35) Back in verse 28, Peter told the people gathered that God had shown him he should not call any man impure or unclean (Acts 10:28). So the card says just what Peter said.
Peter says Jesus Christ "…is Lord of all." (Acts 10:36) He says it right after mentioning the message sent to the people of Israel. And he's saying it in a house full of Gentiles.
Peter does say the message was sent to the people of Israel. But he adds that Jesus Christ "…is Lord of all." (Acts 10:36) That word "all" is doing a lot of work.

Judea comes up in the next verse, where Peter says what happened throughout Judea (Acts 10:37). But when he talks about Jesus's lordship, he says, "…Lord of all." (Acts 10:36) There's no "only" in that sentence.

explanations.answer: Doing good and healing the oppressed
explanations.explanation: Peter says Jesus "…went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil…" (Acts 10:38) Doing good and healing, again and again, all the way around. That's the picture Peter paints.
Peter says nothing about an army. He says Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil (Acts 10:38). The only things being gathered in that verse are good deeds.

Peter doesn't mention that. His words are that Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil (Acts 10:38). If anyone in this passage was known for gifts, it was Cornelius's gifts to the poor (Acts 10:31).

Peter says Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, "…because God was with Him." (Acts 10:38) That's the reason he gives for the doing good and the healing. He names God being with Him, and no other reason.
Peter doesn't say crowds were the reason. He says Jesus did these things "…because God was with Him." (Acts 10:38) The reason Peter gives is God.

Priests aren't part of the reason Peter gives. He says Jesus went around doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him. The reason he names is God being with Jesus (Acts 10:38).
Peter says, "God raised Him up on the third day…" (Acts 10:40) Just that, and nothing about how it happened. Three is the number he gives.
Peter doesn't say the seventh day. He says God raised Jesus up on the third day (Acts 10:40). The seventh day isn't in that verse.
Not the tenth. Peter says God raised Jesus up on the third day (Acts 10:40). No waiting around until day ten.

Peter says it was "…not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand…" (Acts 10:41) God did the choosing, and He did it beforehand. Peter counts himself among them with the word "us."

explanations.answer: The chief priests in the temple
explanations.explanation: Peter doesn't name the chief priests. He says Jesus was seen not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand (Acts 10:41). Peter counts himself among those who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.

Not quite. Peter says Jesus was seen "…not by all the people, but by the witnesses God had chosen beforehand…" (Acts 10:41) So he doesn't say the crowds in Galilee saw Him. The ones who saw Him are the witnesses God had chosen beforehand.
Peter says they weren't far away at all. They were "…us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead." (Acts 10:41) Nobody eats and drinks with someone from across the street.
Right. These witnesses were close. Peter says they were "…us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead." (Acts 10:41) That's a table, not a telescope.

Peter says Jesus "…is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead." (Acts 10:42) God appointed Him, and Peter names both the living and the dead. He is also the Lord of all, as Peter said in verse 36.
There's no "only" in Peter's words. He says God appointed Jesus to judge the living and the dead (Acts 10:42). The Gentile nations aren't named in that sentence at all.
Peter doesn't limit it to Israel. He says Jesus is the One appointed by God to judge the living and the dead (Acts 10:42). Israel isn't named in that sentence at all.

Peter says, "…everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name." (Acts 10:43) Everyone who believes, and it's through His name. Peter says it right after saying that all the prophets testify about Him.
That's not what Peter says. He says everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness of sins through His name (Acts 10:43). Belief is the key word, and he says it to a room that isn't Israel.
Peter doesn't say that. He says, "…everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name." (Acts 10:43) Forgiveness comes through His name, and it goes to everyone who believes.

explanations.answer: The Holy Spirit falls on all who heard
explanations.explanation: Verse 44 says that while Peter was still speaking these words, "…the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard his message." Not some of them, all who heard. The timing is right there in the verse: Peter was still speaking.

explanations.answer: The whole house begins to shake
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't say that. It says the Holy Spirit fell upon all who heard Peter's message while he was still speaking (Acts 10:44). Shaking isn't mentioned.

explanations.answer: An angel appears at the door
explanations.explanation: No angel shows up at the door here. Cornelius had seen a man in radiant clothing days earlier (Acts 10:30). Now it's the Holy Spirit who falls on all who heard Peter's message (Acts 10:44).

explanations.answer: The Spirit was poured out even on the Gentiles
explanations.explanation: The text says the circumcised believers were astounded "…that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles." (Acts 10:45) Gentiles are people who aren't Jews. I think the word "even" says a lot, because the gift reached people they weren't expecting it to reach.

explanations.answer: An angel appeared to the whole household at once
explanations.explanation: No angel is mentioned in this scene. The ones astounded were the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter. They were astounded that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles (Acts 10:45).

explanations.answer: A bright light from heaven filled the whole house
explanations.explanation: The text doesn't mention a light. The ones astounded were the circumcised believers who had accompanied Peter. What astounded them was that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the Gentiles (Acts 10:45).
Verse 46 says they heard them "…speaking in tongues and exalting God." The words they spoke lifted God up. That's the sound that filled the house.
Caesar was Rome's emperor, and he's not who they were praising. Verse 46 says they were speaking in tongues and exalting God. All the praise went to God.

Cornelius is the one who earlier fell at Peter's feet and got helped back up (Acts 10:25-26), so praise for people isn't the theme here. Verse 46 says they were speaking in tongues and exalting God. The praise goes to God.

Peter says the opposite. He says, "They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!" (Acts 10:47) Just as we have, that's his comparison. He's measuring them against himself and the believers with him.
That's it. Peter says, "They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have!" (Acts 10:47) He's pointing at what he just saw. Same Spirit, same gift.

Verse 48 says Peter "…ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ." Earlier in the sermon he'd said that everyone who believes in Jesus receives forgiveness of sins through His name (Acts 10:43). His name is the name that matters here.

John, who proclaimed a baptism and baptized in the Jordan River (Mark 1:4-5), came up in Peter's sermon (Acts 10:37). But the baptisms in Cornelius's house were ordered in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 10:48). John's name isn't the one Peter gave.

Abraham, the ancestor God promised to make into a great nation (Genesis 12:2), isn't named at all in this scene. Peter ordered them baptized in the name of Jesus Christ (Acts 10:48). That's the only name given for the baptisms.
The text says, "Then they asked him to stay for a few days." (Acts 10:48) The verse tells us they asked, and it names a few days. I think that's a house that wasn't ready for the visit to end.
Peter did get an invitation to stay. Verse 48 says, "Then they asked him to stay for a few days." Nobody hurried him out the door.
